notes.high/r0: Best match to the concept's key feature: the upper balcony stands on posts out at the street edge over a deep porch. The stone-and-timber palette is right. Hurt by stray sign blocks floating above the roof and uneven railing posts.
notes.medium/r0: Strong saloon front: a bracketed dark-wood cornice, a small stepped parapet, stone walls framed by timber pilasters, plus barrels and lanterns. The balcony is cantilevered rather than on posts, so it is less faithful to the concept.
notes.medium/r1: Very close to D, with a solid cornice, stone-and-timber walls, a chimney and a layered plank roof. The front is a bit flat and the balcony reads thin.
notes.low/r0: Good stone-and-timber rhythm with a cluttered, lived-in porch and a balcony. The upper-floor window openings render as see-through holes, and the roofline is plain.
notes.low/r1: Lots of layering from stacked beams and cornices, with good relief. The protruding beam ends make it busy and the openings look see-through, so it reads less as a clean saloon.
notes.high/r1: Tidy dark-wood mass with tall timber pilasters and a balcony. The palette is mostly dark wood and loses the concept's grey stone walls, and the roof and eave are generic.
notes.xhigh/r1: Western-style stepped false front with flower pots on the balcony. The flat dirt-coloured roof is exposed, the facade is blocky with a large shadowed central panel, and it looks more like a townhouse than a saloon.
notes.xhigh/r0: Nearly identical to C with the same flat exposed roof and blocky front. Slightly weaker porch and base detail, so it ranks last.

Closest to the concept: grey stone walls between dark wood pilasters, flat roof behind a stone parapet with a stepped false-front, a stone plinth, and a balcony with planters. It reads as a clean, finished storefront. Weak points are the plain flat roof deck and a slightly flat front.
notes.xhigh/r1: Nearly the same build as H with the same strengths. A small chimney and slightly muddier front detailing put it just behind H.
notes.low/r1: Flat roof with a stone rim and layered wood cornice and belt beams gives good horizontal depth and a busy saloon porch. The see-through voids in the upper front and the cluttered ground-floor props make it look less finished.
notes.medium/r1: Good half-timbered stone walls with a balcony, chimney and stepped roof crown, and the craft is solid. The pitched shingle roof makes it read as a Tudor house rather than a flat-fronted western saloon.
notes.medium/r0: Close to F in craft, with timber framing, a balcony and a small stone false-front. The large pitched plank roof and heavy dark front read more medieval inn than frontier saloon.
notes.low/r0: Similar language to B, but the roof is unresolved: part pitched, part flat with a parapet. There are see-through gaps in the front, so it looks unfinished.
notes.high/r0: The only build with a posted veranda holding up the balcony, the concept's signature feature, but it is poorly made: crooked posts, railing stubs floating above the deck, and a sign bar hovering over the roof.
notes.high/r1: Plain box with a heavy flat cornice and two tall centre pilasters. The pale glass-grey infill overwhelms the palette and there is little relief, so it reads as a generic townhouse rather than a saloon.

notes.low/r1: Closest to the concept: grey stone walls between heavy dark-timber posts, a flat roof with a deep cornice, a railed balcony over a furnished porch, and a layered, finished front; it lacks the sign and the corner entry.
notes.low/r0: Similar character and palette to A with good post-and-beam rhythm and a railed balcony; the shallow pitched roof and the tall open voids in the elevation read slightly less finished.
notes.high/r0: The only build with a true posted porch and a railed gallery like the concept, which gives it good depth; the walls are muddy and dark with patchy grey, and the spiky railing tops look odd.
notes.medium/r1: Solid two-storey mass with a timber frame, porch, lanterns and a chimney for interest; the pitched roof and solid balcony band drift from the concept's flat-roofed, railed look.
notes.medium/r0: Similar to H with decent grey-stone infill and a stepped stone crown; the hipped roof and solid wooden balcony fascia make it read more like a townhouse than a saloon.
notes.xhigh/r0: Clean and legible, with paned windows, planters and a railed balcony, but the stone parapet, flat walls and thin porch read as a general store, with little relief.
notes.high/r1: Echoes E's layout but is darker and flatter, with no porch posts, dominant central pilasters and washed-out grey panels; the front lacks a clear saloon entry.
notes.xhigh/r1: A near-copy of D with broken, irregular window openings and a heavy shadow artifact on the front; it reads as unfinished.
